text: The cryoprotective effect of trehalose on boar spermatozoa was investigated by supplementing a base cooling extender with 0, 25, 50, 100 and 200 mmol/l trehalose to improve freeze-thaw tolerance. Motility, acrosome integrity, membrane integrity and cryocapacitation served as evaluation parameters. The optimum was 100 mmol/l, yielding 49.89% motility, 66.52% acrosome integrity and 44.61% membrane integrity; freeze-thawing tolerance was significantly diminished at 200 mmol/l. CTC scores for semen diluted with 100 mmol/l trehalose were 3.68% before and 43.82% after capacitation. Trehalose thus confers greater cryoprotective capacity, significantly improving motility, membrane and acrosome integrity while reducing cryocapacitation during boar spermatozoa cryopreservation.
